I can't be sure I'm the only interviewee, and if it comes down to them picking who gets the job by how much they'll be able to save a year in salary then I don't want to shoot myself in the foot. Should I not talk about money until I know I get the job? I live in the Midwest so Midwesterners you should kind of get an idea on how much someone that does this job makes. Any advice?
New job offer. How much money should I ask for?

Look for a market survey of similar positions in your city/state/whatever. Work out how much experience you have that is directly applicable to your role (not total experience, just the applicable stuff) - the survey will give you a pay range, and this will tell you where in the range you should expect to fall. If you can't find a survey, then look for similar jobs online in your area and see what they pay, or contact job agencies that are advertising these jobs and ask what range you would expect to be paid. I don't know if it applies where you are, but where I am, small businesses always pay considerably less than large ones.

There could be cultural differences (I'm Australian), but I always ask up front what they are willing to pay (before submitting an application; as most of the time I won't be interested). I personally hate asking at interview what the job pays, but if you've made it that far and haven't asked, I would. It's probably worth waiting until they ask you if you have any questions (mentioning it up front may sour them). Assess by their body language and tone how well you think you did, and ask accordingly. If you're desperate for this job, don't go in at the top of the range unless you're sure they love you. This bit is important... In any negotiation, the first person to mention the figure always loses. They may throw the question back on you, "Well, how much do you think you're worth?" Be ready to deflect that however you feel is appropriate.
Often they will ask you what you earned in your last position, and they will aim to pay you about the same (maybe a bit more.) So...lie about how much you've earned in the past I guess
